root_cause_typed.axial_split: the panel CONFIRMS feasibility (viability 3/3 or 2/3 on most failed rows) and REJECTS inventiveness: the modal failed row is fully viable but 0-1/3 non-obvious. The generation-strength rubric measured 'is this a well-formed, physics-correct, quantified solution' (which v18 passes) and NOT 'is this mechanism class distinct from the nearest prior art' (which the frontier judges deny).
root_cause_typed.mechanism_level: the failed rows' mechanism classes are the FIRST-ORDER solution a domain engineer reaches for (coatings, insulation, heat integration, standard separations) — the v18 generator optimizes a mechanism WITHIN the obvious set instead of selecting a mechanism class OUTSIDE it; cross_domain_input was a thin label (aerospace/bio/etc.) applied post-hoc, not a retrieval-constrained mechanism transfer.
root_cause_typed.viability_axis_correction: The 'viability lenient' reading was WRONG at row level: on the 27 failed rows, 22 miss the viability majority (13 at 0/3). The typed viability-fail reasons are FEASIBILITY-AT-SCALE + IMPLEMENTATION-CREDIBILITY (PFPE not stable at 350C, anodization inapplicable to carbon steel, MPa ultrasound not couplable into cloud droplets, oil film not retained under flow): the v18 candidates assert cross-domain mechanisms WITHOUT the domain's implementation constraints. The non-obviousness lever (v19) pulled mechanisms from distant classes but did not carry the transfer-distance cost: the cross-domain precedent's OWN enabling conditions (temperature limits, substrate compatibility, coupling physics) were not checked against the target problem's envelope. THIS is the second binding gap: non-obvious departure must come WITH a feasibility-conservation check (the transferred mechanism's enabling conditions vs the problem envelope), or the panel trades obvious-but-works for novel-but-infeasible.

v19_lever_spec.gate: generation-time NON-OBVIOUSNESS gate: before emitting the final mechanism, the generator must (1) retrieve + cite a CROSS-DOMAIN inspiration mechanism (a mechanism class that solves an analogous constraint in a DIFFERENT domain), (2) state the nearest prior-art mechanism class for the problem's own domain, (3) demonstrate the DEPARTURE: which physical principle differs, why a domain engineer would not reach it by routine adaptation, (4) pass a self-check that the departure is not a mere parameter or material substitution of the prior art.
v19_lever_spec.enforcement: engine-wired prompt contract + parsed departure_section required for emission; physics_truth checks unchanged (DIR 6 intact).
v19_lever_spec.panel_proxy_smoke: 5-problem smoke: the departure sections judged by the panel-proxy (gpt6luna non-obviousness axis) 5/5.
v19_lever_spec.part_b_feasibility_conservation: v19 departure section must ALSO state the precedent's enabling conditions (substrate, temperature window, pressure/coupling regime, scale) and check each against the problem envelope; a departure that fails the check is not emitted (same repair-loop shape as physics_truth).
